newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: S.Africa's Nzo briefs African ministers on Zaire.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa's Nzo briefs African ministers on Zaire.

text.p: South African Foreign Minister Alfred Nzo briefed ministers from 12 southern African states in Zimbabwe on Friday on diplomatic efforts to secure a political settlement in Zaire, Zimbabwe government officials said.
"He gave us an overview of what South Africa, the U.N., the OAU (Organisation of African Unity), the U.S. and France are doing in this direction," a foreign affairs official told Reuters.
"These are efforts we have said in the past we support and that support was pledged again at this meeting," he said, declining to be named.

Nzo used a ministerial meeting of the Southern African Development Community (SADC) on politics, defence and security to discuss the Zairean crisis. President Nelson Mandela is a key player in the search for a peaceful solution.
Nzo was not available for comment after the one-day meeting, called to discuss SADC's charter.
SADC consists of Angola, Botswana, Lesotho, Malawi, Mauritius, Mozambique, Namibia, Tanzania, South Africa, Swaziland, Zambia and Zimbabwe.
At the start of the meeting, the OAU's head of conflict management division, Chris Bakwesegha urged the SADC region to involve the continental body in its programmes.

"SADC as a member of the OAU and U.N. should establish a partnership with these organisations. This partnership should not be used to marginalise others, but to shared responsibilities and vision," he said.
